tracks.title: No Receipt, No Problem
tracks.mood: cocky, petty and laughing at himself
tracks.subject: a Newark guy trying to return a pair of white trainers to a shoe store with no receipt, arguing with the teenage clerk over the scuff on the left toe, and walking out with store credit for exactly one pair of socks
tracks.caption: Jersey club, mid-2020s Newark dance style. Rapid kick-drum triplet patterns and the signature bed-squeak percussion loop; a rubbery sub bass under short bright synth stabs; sharp offbeat handclaps and a cowbell tick. Punchy dry club mix, loud and bouncy, close vocal. Male tenor in a bouncy half-rapped chant, a crew of friends shouting the hook back. 140 BPM, F minor. Cocky, petty and laughing at himself. No trap hi-hat rolls, no autotune, no EDM build-up and drop, no R&B ballad singing, no rock guitars.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - squeak loop and kick triplets]

[Verse 1]
White low-tops, worn them once, I swear
Left toe scuffed but you can't see it there
Box is crushed, the tissue paper's gone
Walk in smiling with my best face on

[Pre-Chorus]
Kid at the counter, maybe seventeen
Looks at the toe, then looks at me

[Chorus]
No receipt, no problem
Paper's in a bin somewhere, forgot it
No receipt, no problem
Hand me the cash and I'll stop talking

[Verse 2]
Says the policy is on the wall
Thirty days, with paper, that is all
I say the paper blew off in the wind
He calls a manager, the manager grins

[Chorus]
No receipt, big problem
Store credit only on a plastic card
No receipt, big problem
Fourteen dollars, wow, that's hard

[Outro - claps and squeak, crew chant]
One pair of socks, brand new, still on the hook
Wearing them now, go on, take a look

tracks.title: Sunday Collars
tracks.subject: a woman teaching her new boyfriend to iron his own work shirts on a Sunday night: steam hissing, collars first, and the one blue shirt he scorches, which she keeps as a nightshirt
tracks.caption: New jack swing revival, late-80s Teddy Riley swing groove with 2020s polish. Swung drum-machine beat with a big gated snare and shuffling hi-hats; a bouncing synth bass; bright DX-style electric piano stabs on the offbeats; slap bass fills and finger snaps between lines. Glossy late-80s mix with modern low end, close lead vocal. Male tenor, smooth R&B lead with stacked falsetto harmonies on the hook. 104 BPM, Bb major. Tender, teasing and quietly smitten. No trap drums, no autotune, no modern pop drop, no rock guitar solo, no ballad tempo.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - gated snare, electric piano stabs, snaps]

[Verse 1]
Sunday night, the board squeaks open wide
Five white shirts are piled up by my side
You fill the iron, tap it twice
Say collars first, I'll say it nice

[Pre-Chorus]
Steam goes hiss across the room
You hum along to the tune

[Chorus]
Collar, cuffs, then the sleeves
Your hand on mine, I don't want to leave
Collar, cuffs, then the back
Keep teaching me slow like that

[Verse 2]
Phone goes off, I turn to look
Smoke comes up like a burning book
My one blue shirt, a brown iron mark
You laugh and say, well, that's your mark

[Chorus]
Collar, cuffs, then the sleeves
You grab the blue one, say it's yours to keep
Collar, cuffs, then the back
You wear it now, I want it back

[Bridge - bass and snaps only]
Monday morning, collar crisp and new
Still smells like Sunday, steam and you

[Outro - stacked falsetto, piano stabs fade]
Collar, cuffs, collar, cuffs
Sunday nights with you are enough

tracks.title: It Comes Back Black
tracks.subject: a London renter at war with a black mould patch on her bathroom ceiling that returns every three weeks no matter how much bleach she uses, until the landlord finally sends someone to fix the extractor fan
tracks.caption: Industrial dark-pop, mid-2020s operatic dance-pop with industrial edges. Distorted four-on-the-floor kick with clanging metallic percussion; a gritty analog synth bass; a fast harpsichord-like synth arpeggio; staccato string stabs on the chorus. Dark glossy dance mix, dry close verses, wide chorus. Female mezzo with low dramatic verses rising to a belted operatic chorus. 122 BPM, D minor. Theatrical, menacing and secretly funny. No trap beat, no autotune, no ballad section, no acoustic guitar, no EDM festival drop.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - metallic hits, synth arpeggio]

[Verse 1]
Above the bath, a little cloud
Grey at first, then shouting loud
I scrub it clean on Sunday night
By Thursday it is back in sight

[Pre-Chorus]
Rubber gloves up to the wrist
Bleach and a sponge in my fist

[Chorus]
It comes back black, it comes back black
I wipe it off, it wipes me back
Three weeks of peace, then the corner cracks
Oh, it comes back black

[Verse 2]
I wrote the landlord twice in May
He said to open windows every day
It's raining and the fan is dead
It hums a note and spins in my head

[Chorus]
It comes back black, it comes back black
Then a man with a ladder, toolbox on his back
He fits a fan that finally works
And the black goes back

[Outro - strings and kick, then one clang]
White ceiling, white tile
Let me look at it a while

tracks.title: Shell on Seven Mile
tracks.subject: a Detroit man whose forty-year-old pet tortoise Big Ron escapes the backyard and is found three blocks away at the car wash on Seven Mile, where the whole crew starts chanting his name
tracks.caption: Detroit ghettotech, fast Detroit club style with electro and booty bass roots. Pounding Roland 808 kick and rapid snare rolls; a deep booty-bass sub; short electro synth stabs; heavy handclaps on every beat. Raw fast club mix, crowded and loud, chants up front. Male MC with chanted call-and-response hooks, a party crowd shouting back. 150 BPM, G minor. Rowdy, silly and party-loud. No trap hi-hats, no autotune, no melodic pop chorus, no house piano, no dubstep wobble.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - 808 kick and claps, MC count-in]

[Verse 1]
Gate swung open in the night
Big Ron gone, there's no shell in sight
Forty years old and he's moving slow
Where did he go, where did he go

[Chorus]
Big Ron, Big Ron, shell on Seven Mile
Big Ron, Big Ron, walking with a style
Slow, slow, slow, slow
Big Ron, Big Ron, where'd you go

[Verse 2]
Lady from the car wash on the phone
Says a tortoise blocking bay number one
Suds on his back and he will not move
Whole line honking, Ron's in the groove

[Chorus]
Big Ron, Big Ron, shell on Seven Mile
Big Ron, Big Ron, foam in his smile
Slow, slow, slow, slow
Big Ron, Big Ron, take it slow

[Bridge - kick and claps only]
Put him in the wagon, put him in the back
Crew on the sidewalk chanting him back

[Outro - crowd chant, kick fades]
Ron, Ron, Ron, Ron
Shined up shell and he's coming home

tracks.title: Garage Line
tracks.subject: a retired bus mechanic in Fresno whose HO-scale model railway grows out of the spare room, across the hallway and through a hole in the garage wall, until his wife's car is parked on the street and she asks for a station named after her
tracks.caption: Surf rock revival, early-60s instrumental surf sound played by a 2020s revival band, with vocals. Reverb-drenched Fender guitar with fast tremolo-picked lead lines; a spring-reverb rhythm guitar chopping eighths; a reedy Farfisa organ; round electric bass; driving surf drums with tom fills. Vintage spring-reverb garage room sound, live-band feel. Male baritone, plain and cheerful, light group 'ooh' backing on the chorus. 150 BPM, E minor. Sunny, frantic and proud. No modern pop production, no distortion-heavy punk, no autotune, no synthesizers, no ballad section.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - tremolo lead guitar and surf drums]

[Verse 1]
Started with a loop on a table top
Little red engine, one small stop
Then the spare room's full of plastic hills
Track on the dresser and the windowsills

[Pre-Chorus]
Drilled a hole through the hallway wall
Train goes by when you take a call

[Chorus]
Garage line, garage line
Running every hour right on time
Through the wall and past the paint
Wife's car out on the street, she's a saint

[Verse 2]
Bridge of balsa over cans of oil
Tiny cows in a box of soil
She stands in the doorway, keys in hand
Asks me where her car is meant to land

[Chorus]
Garage line, garage line
Tunnel where the mower parked, now it's mine
Through the wall and past the paint
Wife's car out on the street, she's a saint

[Bridge - organ and tremolo guitar]
She says build a station, paint it blue
Put my name on it and I'll ride it too

[Outro - surf guitar break, drums fade]
Next stop Linda, ring the bell
Garage line is running well

tracks.title: Setengah Cokelat Setengah Kacang
tracks.subject: a young couple in Bandung at midnight with money for only one martabak manis, arguing chocolate-cheese against peanut at the cart on Dago until they order it half and half and end up feeding each other the other side
tracks.caption: Indonesian spoken-word art pop in the vein of mid-2020s Jakarta storyteller pop. Felt upright piano playing soft repeated chords, a muted electric guitar arpeggio, a warm low synth pad, brushed drum kit with a gentle rimshot, round fretless bass. Intimate bedroom-studio mix with a little tape hiss. Male baritone, half-spoken conversational verses opening into a plainly sung chorus. 84 BPM, D major. Tender, teasing, warm. No autotune, no trap hi-hats, no EDM build, no gospel choir, no stadium drums.

[Intro - felt piano and brushed drums]

[Pre-Chorus]
Aku bilang, kacang dong
Abangnya nunggu, ketawa

[Chorus]
Setengah cokelat, setengah kacang

[Verse 2]

tracks.subject: a boy herding his family's two hundred ducks across a provincial highway at dusk with a bamboo pole and a red bag, while a ten-wheel truck and a pickup wait, and counting them all again on the far bank
tracks.caption: Thai drill, UK-style drill as adopted by Bangkok rappers. Gliding sliding 808 bass, skittering hi-hat triplets and off-grid snares, a dark detuned upright piano riff, short orchestral string stabs, quick snare rolls into each hook. tracks.subject: a couple who set up their first fish tank in a Nonthaburi condo and must wait six weeks for the water to cycle before buying a single betta, testing the water strip together every night
tracks.caption: Thai 2000s-revival alt-rock, the guitar-band sound of early-2000s Bangkok radio brought back by new duos.
